headline: Norway Creates Ocean Sanctuary Spanning 1,848 Square Kilometres
meta_description: Norway establishes its largest marine protected area in Andfjorden, safeguarding coral reefs, kelp forests, and vital fish nurseries.
summary_short: Norway's new marine protected area in Andfjorden covers 1,848.5 square kilometres, shielding diverse ocean ecosystems from human harm.
body:
Norway has created its largest marine protected area in Andfjorden, protecting 1,848.5 square kilometres of ocean. The sanctuary encompasses some of the sea's most vital ecosystems: coral reefs and kelp forests that anchor entire food webs, fish nurseries where young species grow before venturing into open waters, and breeding grounds for whales and seabirds.

This designation marks a significant step in ocean conservation, recognizing that marine life depends on protected spaces free from industrial extraction and other threats. By safeguarding Andfjorden's interconnected habitats—from the smallest nursery grounds to the largest marine mammals—Norway is betting that prevention works better than restoration.
